verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's Computer ecosystem documents a real exec surface on the user's own files: the agent edits files and runs commands behind per-chat approval modes, and its edits and pending approvals appear as tool cards. Open Terminal is listed for running code, and a community comment mentions code execution as a feature. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of command execution and file editing, and detailed docs on the shell/command tool's scope and isolation.

support.subject: As a power user, the assistant can run commands and edit files on my machine — a real exec surface, not just chat about what to do

citations.quote: auto is the everyday setting: the AI can explore freely, but nothing changes on disk and no command runs until you say so.
You see the full history: every file it read, every edit it made, and the pending approval that's blocking it, rendered as tool cards with Allow / Deny buttons.
From zero to your real files in a browser, in about two minutes.
Run Python directly in the browser or via Open Terminal
Files: browse, edit with syntax highlighting, preview Markdown, PDFs, CSVs, and Office files.
